title: A metric with no local isometric immersion
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: A smooth metric on a square can fail to be the metric of any smooth surface in three-dimensional space, on every neighbourhood of a point: this is a theorem of OpenAI (2026), and the course contains a complete proof in seven lessons. Lesson 1: the height equation of an immersed surface, a metric with a given small curvature, and the boundary of a disk of negative curvature. Lesson 2: the construction of the metric and the proof of the theorem from the patch obstruction (P), a statement about the height equation on a fixed square; the metric has the Taylor series of the Euclidean metric at the origin. Lessons 3 to 5: the regularity of admissible heights on the caps of the model square (the linear equation for high derivatives with explicit coefficients, the estimate at a free edge for an equation of mixed type, the induction over the order). Lesson 6: energy estimates where the curvature is negative. Lesson 7: the oscillating perturbation, the moment estimate and the theorem of Baire, which prove (P).
prerequisites: the lesson Submanifolds and hypersurfaces (course Bundles, curvature and holonomy), Proposition A.3: the Gauss formula in coordinates and the Gaussian curvature as det II / det g
core course Real Analysis: differentiation under the integral, uniform convergence of series of derivatives, the inverse function theorem
the lessons prove every other fact they use

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Smooth Metric with No Local Isometric Immersion into Three-Space' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026) was read in full on 12 Oct 2026 (introduction, model, caps, pulse, assembly; 1,512 lines of TeX). Lesson 1 was written against the lemma 'Height equation' (Section 2), the lemma 'Prescribing small curvature' and the lemma 'A negatively curved disk' (Section 5). Every step was derived. The lesson adds: the transformation rules under affine maps with proof, a complete proof of the smoothness of the solution of f_XX = -K_0 f in both variables (the manuscript refers to smooth dependence on a parameter), and the reduction of an immersion that is a graph to the graph of a function (the manuscript uses the formula for graphs directly). Checked in exact arithmetic before staging (plan/checks_20261012/ni_check_heights.py): K = -f_XX/f from the coordinate formula; for a polynomial graph and four vectors e, the Gauss equation, Hess z = nu II, the height equation and nu^2 + |dz|^2 = |e|^2; the rules H' = lambda^2 R^T H R, E' = lambda^4 E, K' = K under an affine map. No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 2 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the definitions and the statement of the proposition 'Patch obstruction' in Section 2 and against Section 5 (placement and smooth summation, the proof of the main theorem, the corollary on the Euclidean Taylor jet). Every step of Section 5 was derived. The lesson makes the placement explicit (circles of radius rho_j (1 + 2^-k) with A 2^k equally spaced centres and rotations assigned cyclically; the inequalities for disjointness are verified), gives the bound for the push-forward of a perturbation with its constant, and states the consequence of the proposition that the construction uses as statement (P). No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 3 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the lemmas 'Curvature drift' and 'High derivative equation' of Section 3. Every identity was derived; the terms written O(K) in the manuscript are explicit in the lesson (rho_1, rho_2, rho, and the multiple of K in C). Checked by computer algebra before staging: plan/checks_20261012/ni_check_commutation.py (the commutation of third derivatives with its sign, exact, three random metrics), ni_check_drift.py (the drift identity with rho_1 and rho_2, exact, on the height of a polynomial graph at three points; the partial derivatives of P, symbolic), ni_check_multiplier.py (the formula for D^2 and the differentiated equation, symbolic). The manuscript's formulas agree with the explicit ones. Lesson 4 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the lemma 'The free cap edge' of Section 3, as a statement about a general equation u_tt + A u_ss + B u_t + C u_s = f with three assumptions (A1)-(A3); every constant is explicit (lambda, c_1, c_2 of Proposition 3.1; the bounds of the elliptic estimate). The multiplier identity with its fluxes, the three weight formulas and the elliptic test identity were checked by computer algebra (plan/checks_20261012/ni_check_multiplier.py). The manuscript's argument was followed step by step; its order of choices (epsilon, lambda, c_1) and its exponent p = 8 are kept. No discrepancy; the manuscript states the elliptic error bound as C(1 + d^(p-5)), the lesson obtains the bound with exponents p - 4 and p - 3, which is also sufficient. Lesson 5 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the proposition 'Cap regularity' of Section 3 and the proofs of the lemmas 'High derivative equation' (remainder bound) and 'The free cap edge' (verification of the hypotheses in the cap). Every step was derived: flow coordinates on [-2, 2]^2 with bi-Lipschitz bounds; the verification of (A1)-(A3) with the explicit choice of a_0 and theta_0 (compactness of the zero set of the curvature in the cap; the point (0, -1) where K_y is not zero); the count of high-order factors (2(l - 3) > l); the recovery of the derivatives with more x-indices; the reflection for the upper cap. A Sobolev inequality on squares is proved in the lesson. No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 6 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the first two parts of Section 4 (the bounded solution class with the sheared coordinates, and the lemma 'Propagation to the pulse'). Every step was derived. The equation for the derivatives along xi is obtained from the theorem of lesson 3 by exchanging the two coordinates, which gives P_1 = 2(q - q_0)/d_0 and S_1 = -1/d_0 as in the manuscript; the speed bound |P_1| + sqrt(S_1) < 2/v_* <= L/4 and the energy identity were recomputed; the constant of the energy inequality is explicit (c_E = 3 beta_1 (1 + 1/s_min)). A first draft had c_E = beta_1 (2 + 3/s_min), which is too small when s_min > 3; corrected before staging. No discrepancy with the manuscript. Lesson 7 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the rest of Section 4 (the test metrics, the comparison across the thin strip, the curvature forcing and its moment, the category argument). Every step was derived, with the constants that must not depend on delta tracked (c_D, C_D, s_2, C_5, C_6, c_3). The lesson adds a proof of the completeness of the space of perturbations and of the theorem of Baire for open subsets, the choice of the slab with the bound |s - theta| <= r/10 (the manuscript states r/4 and remarks that r/10 holds), and the construction of the comparison polynomial. No discrepancy with the manuscript. With this lesson every step of Sections 2 to 5 of the manuscript has been derived and written out in the course.

open_obligations: None for the main theorem: Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 6.1 of the second lesson are proved from the patch obstruction, which is Theorem 1.3 of the seventh lesson.

Standard facts used by name and not proved in the course: the inverse function theorem, existence and smooth dependence of solutions of ordinary differential equations on initial values (for the flow coordinates), differentiation under the integral, the formula of Taylor with remainder, and the Gauss formula and Gauss equation for surfaces, which are Proposition A.3 of the lesson Submanifolds and hypersurfaces of the course Bundles, curvature and holonomy.
Statements that the course relays from the manuscript's introduction without checking them: the history of the problem (Yau, Ghomi, Janet-Cartan, Nakamura-Maeda, Nadirashvili-Yuan).
